name: AD8597 / AD8599 (single/dual ultralow-noise, ultralow-distortion bipolar)
tagline: ADI's bipolar single and dual, rated 1.1 nV/rtHz and -120 dB THD at 1 kHz. Head-Fi op-amp rollers called the AD8599 'bloody good': dynamic and sparkling.
technology: Bipolar-input voltage-feedback op amp made only by Analog Devices. The ADI AD8597 macro-model's generic description reads '9/30V, BIP, OP, Low THD, Low Noise, 1X'. The ADI behavioural model has input clamp diodes: two anti-parallel strings of two series diodes (D1-D2 and D3-D4) across the inputs. The data sheet specifies operation from +/-4.5 V, and the AD8599-EP data sheet gives an absolute maximum supply of +/-18 V. The fab is not verified. PCN 25_0091 (2025) qualifies ADI's Camas, WA fab for ADI bipolar products, but no search result showed that this family is on its list.

part_numbers.notes: Single. Orderables in a 2026 part-index sitemap: AD8597ARZ, AD8597ARZ-REEL and AD8597ARZ-REEL7 (SOIC-8), plus AD8597ACPZ-R2, AD8597ACPZ-REEL and AD8597ACPZ-REEL7 (8-lead LFCSP_VD, 3 x 3 mm). The ADI product page exists (analog.com/en/products/ad8597.html). ADI PCNs 10_0004, 14_0038 and 17_0068 (cancelled) list AD8597 variants. The ADI lifecycle status was not verified by search.

Dual, standard dual-op-amp pinout. Orderables: AD8599ARZ, AD8599ARZ-REEL and AD8599ARZ-REEL7 (SOIC-8 only; there is no DIP, so socket rolling needs an SOIC-to-DIP adapter). The ADI product page exists, and Arrow and Octopart list AD8599ARZ. Farnell order code 1438872 (from a ColdMatter Eagle board). The ADI lifecycle status was not verified by search.

Enhanced Product version, also sold as AD8599TRZ-EP-R7. It has its own data sheet, AD8599-EP Rev. 0 (revision history: '8/15 - Revision 0: Initial Version'), with an absolute maximum supply of +/-18 V. The temperature grade and spec differences from the commercial AD8599 were not checked.

lineage.notes: The AD8599 came first, with its own dual-only data sheet ('Dual, Ultralow Distortion, Ultralow Noise Op Amp AD8599', Rev. A, 2007, per the bdtic.com mirror). The ADI macro-model header reads 'AD8599 DMod model March 12 2007, D.F. Bowers'. The single AD8597 was added later, under the combined AD8597/AD8599 data sheet. Eagle's ChangeLog cites AD8597_8599.pdf on 2009-12-22, and the AD8597 macro-model is dated 05/2010. The combined data sheet is now at Rev. F. No second sources are known.
The AD8599-EP data sheet Rev. 0 is the initial version, dated 8/15. Its orderables are AD8599TRZ-EP and AD8599TRZ-EP-R7.

reputation.summary: On Head-Fi, the AD8599 is best known from the 'AD8599 is bloody good' thread, where op-amp rollers call it dynamic, vivacious, sparkling and 'alive'. One comparison thread calls it warmer than other Analog Devices op amps, with an accurate soundstage. Both come from the discovery notes, and neither thread was re-read in this pass. Engineers use it as an ultralow-noise, ultralow-distortion bipolar dual: 1.1 nV/rtHz and -120 dB THD at 1 kHz per ADI. Its claimed role as a low-noise alternative to the OPA1612 and LME49720 comes only from discovery notes (unverified). Uses confirmed in GitHub-hosted designs: the output amp of a DAC8812 MDAC volume attenuator (FutureSharks preamp-two); the RX I/Q or AF preamp in Elecraft KX3 and KX2 transceivers, next to the OPA2209; the I/Q baseband amp in the T41/Phoenix SDR; and precision low-noise instrumentation front ends. No ASR or Samuel Groner measurements were retrieved.
sonic_descriptors: warmer than other Analog Devices op amps
typical_uses: Op-amp rolling in DAC and headphone-amp sockets (via SOIC-to-DIP adapter)
Output amplifier for multiplying-DAC (MDAC) volume attenuators in DIY preamps
Low-noise line and headphone preamplifier stages with low source impedance
SDR I/Q baseband and RX AF preamp stages (Elecraft KX3/KX2, T41/Phoenix SDR)
Precision low-noise instrumentation and ADC driver front ends
caveats: The dual is SOIC-8 only (no DIP), so socket rolling needs an adapter. Adapter layout and decoupling can affect stability.
It needs split rails of at least +/-4.5 V and must stay within the +/-18 V absolute maximum, so it does not suit low-voltage single-supply portable designs.
Low voltage noise helps only at low source impedance. With a bipolar input, current noise and bias current matter with high-impedance sources (no AD8599 i_n or I_B figures verified).
The input clamp diodes in ADI's model suggest a limited differential input voltage. Check the data sheet's absolute maximum ratings before using it in circuits with large input steps.
Community sound descriptors are subjective forum impressions (low confidence), and the forum threads were not re-read.

counterfeit_notes: No AD8597/AD8599-specific counterfeit or remarking reports were found. No search was spent on this in this pass. The AD8599 comes only in SOIC-8, and the AD8597 in SOIC-8 or LFCSP, sold mainly through authorised ADI distribution. By inference, treat any DIP-8 'AD8599' as a relabel or an adapter assembly. Buy from authorised distributors. To check a suspect part on the bench, look for e_n of about 1.1 nV/rtHz and very low THD. A relabelled 5532- or 4580-class die would measure clearly noisier and more distorted.
alternatives: TI OPA1612 (1.1 nV/rtHz bipolar dual, the usual comparison)
ADI ADA4898-2 (lower-noise bipolar dual; one ColdMatter Eagle design places an ADA4898-2 on the AD8599 SOIC footprint)
TI OPA2209 (precision low-noise dual, used next to the AD8599 in Elecraft KX2/KX3 and T41 SDRs)

revision_chain_notes:
I used all 6 web searches. The AD8597/AD8599 revision chain, oldest to newest:

1. **AD8599 Rev. 0 (dual only, 2007).** Missing: no copy found, date unknown.
2. **AD8599 Rev. A (dual only, 2007).** Already known: the bdtic copy.
3. **AD8597 Rev. PrA (single only, preliminary).** New: datasheetbank has pages for it. The already-listed Farnell copy (1877551.pdf) is this preliminary AD8597 sheet, not a combined revision. Its record should be corrected to doc AD8597, Rev. PrA. Date unknown.
4. **AD8597/AD8599 Rev. B (2008, copyright 2007-2008).** This is the first combined single/dual edition. New: the datasheetbank RevB page. The already-listed Marutsu copy is also Rev. B.
5. **Rev. C.** New: the manualmachine.com copy. Date unknown.
6. **Rev. D.** Missing: no copy and no date found.
7. **Rev. E.** New: the datasheetq copy. Date unknown.
8. **Rev. F (08/20/2015 per metadata).** Already known: analog.com and radiolocman di=170475.

AD8599-EP Rev. 0 (8/15) is a separate document and is already known.

These copies do not show their revision:
- Octopart cache (AD8597ARZ): the 'Data Sheet' title style suggests D, E or F.
- Alldatasheet AD8597 (ID 250052).
- Datasheetcafe.
- Scribd.

Still missing:
- Dates for Rev. C, Rev. D and Rev. E.
- Any copy of AD8599 Rev. 0 and of AD8597/AD8599 Rev. D.
- The full revision-history table in the Rev. F data sheet, which would give the date and changes for each step (B to C, C to D, D to E, E to F).

Wayback captures of the legacy URL http://www.analog.com/static/imported-files/data_sheets/AD8597_8599.pdf, from about 2009 to 2015, are the best route to Rev. C, D and E.
